text:
ashwin: heads up — started seeing a cluster-wide spike in Pending GPU pods about 10m ago. Lots of small-ish pods can't schedule even though we have spare GPU capacity in some node pools. logs point at fragmentation + CA not launching new nodes. 

infra-bot: [autoscaler] 2026-03-18T11:04:22Z scale_up: skipped scaling; reason: no capacity for requested instance types.

jordan: can you paste one of the Pending events?

ashwin: sure — example from a failed pod: 
```
Events:
  Type     Reason     Age   From               Message
  ----     ------     ----  ----               -------
  Warning  FailedScheduling  2m   default-scheduler  0/72 nodes are available: 72 Insufficient nvidia.com/gpu, 45 node(s) had volume node affinity conflict.
```
It looks like CA sees the gpu SKU gap and doesn't bring up new nodes due to instance quota exhaustion in eu-west2. but also fragmentation: many nodes have 1 GPU free but pod requests 2 GPUs.

sara: quick q — are these pods strictly requesting whole GPUs or using fractional annotations (MIG/partition)?

miguel: they request whole GPUs: `resources.requests: nvidia.com/gpu: 2`. Most of our ML jobs are >1 GPU and the cluster is a mix of 4xA100 and 1xV100 nodes. Binpacking WRT different capacities is killing fit.

ops_lead: CA will only scale if a new node type would satisfy the unschedulable pod. We have many small leftover 1-GPU slots because of mixed node sizes. Two angles: 1) change pod requests to be packable (`request: 1` with multi-container co-scheduling), or 2) adjust node pool flavors to be more homogeneous / add a dedicated pool for 2+ GPU jobs. Both have tradeoffs (cost vs throughput).

jordan: also see this in the CA logs: 
```
I0318 11:02:13 cluster-autoscaler: NoOptionsForNode: no options for node: instanceQuotaExceeded
I0318 11:02:13 cluster-autoscaler: ScaleDown: skipped, recently unneeded
```
So quota is part of it. Could be spot mix too — recently we've seen spot churn in us-west causing migrations that reduce usable slots.

ashwin: thought: can we add a taint/toleration-based dedicated pool (reserved, on-demand) for multi-GPU training? Keep it small but always up. That would cost more but reduce failures and retries. 

miguel: +1 for a small reserved 2x-A100 pool. We can also try a temporary scheduling shim: use `podTopologySpread` + `nodeSelector` to prefer nodes with contiguous free GPUs. Hacky but quick.

infra-bot: [quota-check] account eu-west2: GPU quota remaining: 0/40 for A100, spot quota 12/20 used.

ops_lead: action items: 
- miguel to open infra ticket to request +20 A100 quota in eu-west2 (priority)
- jordan to propose nodepool for reserved 2x-GPU on-demand nodes (small size, 3 nodes)
- ashwin to add a short-term admission hook suggestion doc for scheduling-friendly resource requests

jordan: cost note — moving 3 on-demand 2x-A100 nodes ~ +$14k/month. If we get quota it might be cheaper to consolidate a few spot pools with same SKU to reduce fragmentation.

ashwin: will run an experiment now: try launching a 3-node dedicated pool and reproduce scheduling for one of the failing jobs, update in 20m. :eyes:

miguel: if someone hits it meanwhile, try editing the job to request 1 GPU (if acceptable) or set `nodeAffinity` to the nodepool with >1 contiguous GPUs. Also thinking long-term: enable MIG/partitioning for A100s we control so we can pack 2x1-GPU pods into a single physical GPU where supported.

ops_lead: thanks team. please keep channel updated. i'll flag leadership for emergency quota request if CA doesn't get unblocked after the reserved pool test. :thumbsup:
